sounds.name: First Acid
sounds.ref: In the style of late 1980s Chicago acid house
sounds.blurb: A plain acid line: a sawtooth that squelches on every note and jumps out on the accents.
sounds.how: One sawtooth goes through a resonant low-pass filter. DEPTH lets the envelope flick the filter open on each note and DECAY closes it again, and RESONANCE turns that movement into a squelch. Accented steps play louder and open the filter further; slid steps glide into the next note.

steps.title: A sawtooth, filter fairly low
steps.why:
Everything starts with the one oscillator. The sawtooth carries every harmonic, so it gives the filter the most to work on.
- WAVE sawtooth: bright and buzzy.
- CUTOFF 3.5 (about 520 Hz): low, so between notes the sound is dark.
- RESONANCE 2 and DEPTH 2: almost no squelch yet.
- Listen for: play the riff. It is a dull, plodding bass for now.

steps.title: Turn up the resonance
steps.why:
RESONANCE boosts the frequencies at the cutoff point. On a 303-style filter that is the squelch.
- RESONANCE 8: a strong, vocal peak that follows the filter as it moves.
- Listen for: each note now has a rubbery "yow". Turn RESONANCE back to 2 and the line goes plain again.

steps.title: Let the envelope open it
steps.why:
DEPTH sets how far the envelope opens the filter on each note before DECAY closes it. With high resonance that sweep is the acid sound.
- DEPTH 6: a big sweep on every note.
- DECAY 3.5 (about 340 ms): each note closes fairly quickly, so the line stays tight.
- Listen for: the squelch gets wider. Turn DECAY up and the notes smear into long "wows".

steps.title: Accents
steps.why:
The riff has accented steps. ACCENT sets how much they stand out: louder, and with an extra sweep of the filter that grows with RESONANCE.
- ACCENT 7: the accented notes jump out with a sharp shriek.
- Listen for: the pattern of loud and quiet notes. Turn ACCENT to 0 and the line goes flat.

context.vcf.resonance: The squelch. Most acid lines live between 7 and 10.
context.vcf.cutoff: Sweep this slowly while the riff plays. That slow sweep is how acid tracks build.
context.vcf.depth: How far each note opens. Low values keep the line dark, so the accents stand out more.
context.env.decay: How long each note takes to close. Short is tight and plucky; long smears the notes together.
context.vca.accent: How hard the accented steps hit.

tweaks.try: Sweep slowly from 2 to 8 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: The line opens from a muffled thud into a screaming squelch.
The same line, thicker and angrier.

sounds.name: Saturated Acid
sounds.ref: In the style of mid-1990s acid techno
sounds.blurb: A hard, driven acid line pushed through the B1’s saturation until the resonance screams.
sounds.how: The acid voice with the resonance near the top and a long decay, run into the saturation. Saturation squashes the loud and quiet parts together, so the squelch stays loud as the filter closes and the resonant peak turns into a scream. TONE sets how harsh the scream is.

steps.title: A squelchy start
steps.why:
Set up a strong acid voice first, so the saturation has a peak to work on.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 4, RESONANCE 9: a sharp, ringing peak.
- DEPTH 5, DECAY 5 (about 510 ms): each note opens and closes slowly.
- ACCENT 6: the accents stand out.
- Listen for: a loud, wet squelch, still clean.

steps.title: Switch the saturation on
steps.why:
SATURATION comes after the VCA, so it shapes the whole note.
- SATURATION on, DRIVE 7: the line is pushed hard into the clipper.
- Listen for: the notes get louder and longer, and the quiet ends of each note are lifted up.

steps.title: Shape the scream with TONE
steps.why:
TONE is a brightness control after the clipping. Turned up, it lets the harsh new harmonics through.
- TONE 7: a bright, cutting scream on every accent.
- Listen for: the top end biting. Turn TONE to 2 for a darker, woollier roar.

context.sat.drive: How hard the line is pushed. Above 8 the notes blur into one roar.
context.sat.tone: Turn right for a harsher, brighter scream.
context.vcf.resonance: Near the top so the saturation has a peak to scream with.

tweaks.hear: The build-up of a 90s acid track, from rumble to scream.
Just a little grit; the squelch comes back into focus.

sounds.name: Dub Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of slow, dub-influenced acid
sounds.blurb: A sparse, rubbery line that the delay throws back and forth into the gaps.
sounds.how: A slow acid voice with plenty of room between the notes. The delay is set to about three sixteenths at this tempo, so each echo lands off the beat, and FEEDBACK keeps the echoes coming. The line is written sparse so the echoes have space.

steps.title: A round, slow voice
steps.why:
Dub likes a fat, soft bass, with the squelch kept low.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 3, RESONANCE 6: dark with a gentle peak.
- DEPTH 4, DECAY 6 (about 690 ms): each note opens softly and dies slowly.
- Listen for: a slow, rubbery line with lots of space.

steps.title: Turn the delay on
steps.why:
The delay repeats the sound after the saturation, so it echoes whatever you hear.
- DELAY on, TIME 9 (about 390 ms): close to three sixteenths at 96 BPM, so the echoes fall off the beat.
- LEVEL 5: the echoes sit a little under the dry line.
- FEEDBACK 0: one echo per note.
- Listen for: every note answered once, in the gaps.

steps.title: Feed it back
steps.why:
FEEDBACK sends the echo back into the delay, so each echo makes another, quieter one.
- FEEDBACK 6: four or five echoes that fade away.
- Listen for: the line turns into a cloud of repeats. Above 9 the echoes take a long time to die; drop it when the cloud gets muddy.

context.dly.time: Set it so the echoes land on a beat or off it. Small changes while it plays make a pitch-bending warble.
context.dly.feedback: How many echoes. The higher, the longer the tail.
context.dly.level: How loud the echoes are against the dry line.

tweaks.try: Turn TIME slowly while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: The echoes slide in pitch as the delay stretches: the classic dub warble.

sounds.name: Ratchet Roll
sounds.ref: In the style of modern acid techno
sounds.blurb: A driving line with rolls: some steps play two, three or four times inside their own length.
sounds.how: RATCHET repeats a step inside its own length. Here some steps play twice, some three or four times, so the line stutters into the next beat. A short decay keeps each repeat crisp, and a little saturation glues them together.

steps.title: A tight, short voice
steps.why:
Ratchets only work if each repeat is heard on its own, so the notes have to be short.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 4.5, RESONANCE 7, DEPTH 5.
- DECAY 2 (about 215 ms): each note closes quickly.
- ACCENT 6.
- Listen for: the rolls ticking clearly, like a drum roll on the bass.

steps.title: Hear what DECAY does to a roll
steps.why:
With a long decay the repeats run into each other and the roll turns into a smear.
- DECAY 5: about half a second.
- Listen for: the rolls blurring into single, wobbling notes. Bring it back down when you have heard it.

steps.title: Back to tight, with some grit
steps.why:
A little saturation makes the repeats sound like one instrument.
- DECAY 2.5: crisp again.
- SATURATION on, DRIVE 4, TONE 5: some warmth and weight, not a scream.
- Listen for: a punchy, rolling line that sits on the beat.

context.env.decay: Keep it short, or the repeats run into each other.
context.vcf.depth: More DEPTH and every repeat squelches.

tweaks.hear: Each repeat in a roll gets its own squelch.
The rolls echo into one another.

sounds.name: Square Bounce
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s electro bass lines
sounds.blurb: A hollow, bouncing square-wave bass with short notes and plenty of space.
sounds.how: The square wave has only odd harmonics, so it sounds hollow and woody next to the sawtooth. Short GATE LENGTHs leave gaps between the notes, which is what makes the line bounce, and the occasional long note holds a beat down.

steps.title: Switch to the square wave
steps.why:
WAVE picks the oscillator’s shape. The square has half the harmonics of the sawtooth, all the odd ones.
- WAVE square: hollow and woody.
- CUTOFF 4.5, RESONANCE 3: the filter softens it a little without squelching.
- Listen for: a rounder, more muted bass than a sawtooth.

steps.title: Short notes for bounce
steps.why:
The riff uses short gate lengths on most steps and a long one now and then. DECAY is kept short so the short notes stay short.
- DECAY 2: a quick pluck.
- DEPTH 5: a small "pop" at the start of each note.
- Listen for: the gaps between the notes. They are as much a part of the groove as the notes.

context.vco.wave: Flip to sawtooth and the same line turns brighter and buzzier.
context.env.decay: Longer and the notes lose their bounce.

tweaks.hear: The line moves up a fourth, still in tune with itself.
The pop at the start of each note turns into a quick "bip".

sounds.name: Gliding Line
sounds.ref: In the style of early 1990s acid trance
sounds.blurb: A long, singing line where most notes slide into the next.
sounds.how: A slid step is held into the next one, so the pitch glides there without starting the envelope again. With most of the steps slid, the line sings in one long, rising and falling breath; the few un-slid notes give it a pulse.

steps.title: A singing voice
steps.why:
A slide only sings if the note is long enough to hear it, so the decay is longer than usual.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 5, RESONANCE 7, DEPTH 4.
- DECAY 6: long notes.
- Listen for: the pitch gliding between most of the notes.

steps.title: Slide everything you play
steps.why:
The riff’s slides are written into its steps. SLIDE does the same for the notes you play yourself.
- SLIDE lit: every note you play glides from the one before.
- Listen for: play a few keys on the keyboard while the riff is stopped. Each one glides in. Switch SLIDE off and the notes jump.

context.env.decay: Long, so a slid note has time to glide.
context.seq.slide: Lit, every note you play glides; the riff slides only where it is written to.

tweaks.hear: The singing line opening up into a trance lead.
The glides trail off into echoes.

sounds.name: Deep Sub
sounds.ref: In the style of deep house bass lines
sounds.blurb: A dark, round bass with the filter almost shut and no squelch.
sounds.how: Not every bass needs to squelch. With CUTOFF low, RESONANCE and DEPTH down, the B1 gives a dark, warm bass that sits under a track. The square wave down low is close to a pure tone, felt as much as heard.

steps.title: Close the filter
steps.why:
A low CUTOFF lets through only the lowest harmonics.
- WAVE square, CUTOFF 2 (about 300 Hz): dark and round.
- RESONANCE 1, DEPTH 1: no peak and almost no movement.
- DECAY 6: long, steady notes.
- Listen for: a warm, heavy bass with no squelch at all.

steps.title: A touch of warmth
steps.why:
Low saturation adds harmonics that let a deep bass be heard on small speakers.
- SATURATION on, DRIVE 2, TONE 3.
- Listen for: the same bass, a little fuller, especially on headphones or laptop speakers.

context.vcf.cutoff: Keep it under 3 for a sub bass; open it for more bite.
context.sat.drive: A little makes it heard on small speakers; a lot makes it a different sound.

tweaks.hear: A gentle "wow" creeps into each note.

sounds.name: Acid Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of acid house leads
sounds.blurb: The B1 played high: a whistling, resonant lead with echoes behind it.
sounds.how: The same voice an octave or two up turns from a bass into a lead. PITCH tunes the whole line up by seven semitones, high RESONANCE makes it whistle, and the delay gives the phrase space.

steps.title: Tune it up
steps.why:
PITCH tunes the oscillator up to seven semitones either way.
- PITCH +7: a fifth up.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 5.5, RESONANCE 8, DEPTH 5, DECAY 4.
- Listen for: a bright, whistling line, higher than any of the basses.

steps.title: Give it echoes
steps.why:
A lead with gaps sounds bigger with the delay filling them.
- DELAY on, TIME 8 (about 300 ms), LEVEL 4, FEEDBACK 4.
- Listen for: each phrase answered by a trail of echoes.

context.vco.pitch: The whole line moves; the riff itself is already up high.
context.vcf.resonance: The whistle. Up high it can get piercing, so watch MASTER.

tweaks.hear: Long, singing notes that overlap their echoes.

sounds.name: Resonant Zaps
sounds.ref: In the style of the zaps and blips of early acid house
sounds.blurb: Laser zaps: the filter ringing on its own, swept down fast on every note.
sounds.how: With RESONANCE right up the filter rings at its cutoff like a second oscillator. DEPTH at the top makes the envelope sweep that ring from high to low in a moment, and a very short DECAY makes it a zap. Ratchets fire bursts of zaps.

steps.title: Make the filter ring
steps.why:
At the top of RESONANCE the filter rings on its own.
- RESONANCE 10, CUTOFF 2: a low, ringing note under the sawtooth.
- WAVE sawtooth, DEPTH 3, DECAY 3.
- Listen for: a whistle on every note.

steps.title: Sweep it fast
steps.why:
The zap is the ring swept from high to low very quickly.
- DEPTH 10: the envelope throws the cutoff right to the top.
- DECAY 1 (about 160 ms): and drops it straight back.
- Listen for: "pew" on every note.

steps.title: Accents make bigger zaps
steps.why:
ACCENT adds its own sweep of the filter, so the accented zaps go further.
- ACCENT 10.
- DELAY on, TIME 6, FEEDBACK 5, LEVEL 4: the zaps bounce into the distance.
- Listen for: the accented zaps jumping out above the others.

context.vcf.resonance: Keep at the top: the zap is the ring.
context.env.decay: Shorter for a click, longer for a "peeow".

tweaks.hear: Each zap turns into a slower, falling whistle.
The zaps start higher and end on a squelch.

sounds.name: Gated Stabs
sounds.ref: A sequencer technique: gate length as the groove
sounds.blurb: One note, the groove written entirely in gate lengths, accents and rests.
sounds.how: Every step is the same pitch. What changes is how long each one is held (GATE LENGTH), which are accented, and where the rests fall. With a long DECAY the gate length is what cuts each note off, so short, normal and long gates sound clearly different.

steps.title: A long voice, so the gate decides
steps.why:
With a long DECAY the note keeps sounding until its gate ends, so the gate lengths in the pattern are what you hear.
- WAVE sawtooth, CUTOFF 4, RESONANCE 7, DEPTH 4.
- DECAY 7: long.
- Listen for: some notes clipped short, some held. Same pitch every time, still a groove.

steps.title: Shorten DECAY and lose it
steps.why:
Once DECAY is shorter than the shortest gate, every note dies on its own and the gate lengths stop mattering.
- DECAY 1.
- Listen for: the groove going flat, every note the same click. Turn DECAY back up to bring the gate lengths back.

steps.title: Back up, with saturation
steps.why:
Saturation makes the held notes louder for longer, so the long gates stand out more.
- DECAY 6.
- SATURATION on, DRIVE 5, TONE 6.
- Listen for: a pumping, stabbing groove on one note.

context.env.decay: Longer than the gates, or the gate lengths cannot be heard.
context.vca.accent: The accents carry the groove along with the gate lengths.

tweaks.hear: One note, but the whole groove opening and closing.
The stabs transpose, as the B1’s keys transpose a playing pattern.

sounds.name: Dotted-Eighth Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of The Edge
sounds.blurb: Plain eighth notes that the delay turns into a chiming, galloping sixteenth pattern.
sounds.how: The Edge played simple eighth notes into a delay set to a dotted eighth, so every repeat fell between the notes he played and the guitar seemed to play twice as fast. At 100 BPM a dotted eighth is 450 ms, so the delay TIME goes near the top.

steps.title: A plucked tone
steps.why:
A sawtooth with the cutoff part way up and some DEPTH, so each note has a bright pick.
- WAVE Sawtooth
- CUTOFF 5 · 917 Hz
- RESONANCE 2
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 3.5
- DECAY 3.5 · 330 ms: the one envelope also sets how long the note sounds
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: plain, plucked eighth notes.

steps.title: The dotted echo
steps.why:
The delay repeats each note three-sixteenths later, which lands it between the next two notes. A little feedback adds a second, quieter repeat.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 9.5 · 440 ms: about a dotted eighth at 100 BPM
- Delay FEEDBACK 3
- Delay LEVEL 6: loud enough to sound like part of the riff
- Listen for: the eighths turn into a chiming, galloping sixteenth pattern.

context.dly.time: Set to the beat: a different TIME and the gallop falls apart.

tweaks.hear: The echo lands on the off-beat sixteenth and the gallop becomes a stutter.
You hear how plain the part really is.

sounds.name: Black Ark Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of Lee “Scratch” Perry
sounds.blurb: A deep, warm dub bass whose accents throw long echoes into the room.
sounds.how: Lee Perry’s Black Ark studio soaked everything in tape echo and saturation. A round, saturated bass with a long echo that keeps feeding back, so the accents hang in the air.

steps.title: Round bass
steps.why:
A square into a low cutoff with a little DEPTH; a long decay so each note sustains.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 2 · 297 Hz
- RESONANCE 1
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 2
- DECAY 7 · 920 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a deep, round bass.

steps.title: Tape warmth
steps.why:
Saturation with a dark tone, like a tape machine driven hot.
- SATURATION ON/OFF On
- Saturation DRIVE 5
- Saturation TONE 3
- Listen for: a warmer, thicker bass.

steps.title: The Ark
steps.why:
An eighth-note echo at 72 BPM is about 420 ms. High feedback keeps it repeating.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 9.4 · 430 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 6.5: high, so the echoes keep coming back
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: a deep bass trailing long, fading echoes.

context.dly.feedback: High feedback is the Black Ark sound; turn it down and the room gets smaller.

tweaks.hear: The echoes pile up and nearly run away.

sounds.name: Far East Melodica
sounds.ref: In the style of Augustus Pablo
sounds.blurb: A reedy, minor-key melodica melody floating in echo.
sounds.how: Augustus Pablo played haunting minor melodies on the melodica over dub, his “Far East” sound. A reedy square, PITCH set to put it in key, and a long echo.

steps.title: Reed
steps.why:
A square with a middle cutoff and a touch of resonance is reedy, like a melodica. A long decay sustains the notes.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 5 · 917 Hz
- RESONANCE 3
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 1
- DECAY 8 · 1.2 s
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a reedy, wheezy tone.

steps.title: Echo chamber
steps.why:
At 76 BPM an eighth is about 390 ms; medium feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 9 · 390 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 5
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: a haunting melody trailing echoes.

sounds.name: E2-E4 Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of Manuel Göttsching — E2-E4
sounds.blurb: A gently pulsing two-chord sequence that echoes into a long, hypnotic shimmer.
sounds.how: Göttsching’s hour-long E2-E4 rocks between two chords over a steady sequence while echoes multiply. A soft pluck and an echo that fills the gaps.

steps.title: Soft pluck
steps.why:
A saw with a middle cutoff, some DEPTH and gentle resonance; a medium decay.
- WAVE Sawtooth
- CUTOFF 4 · 629 Hz
- RESONANCE 3
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 3
- DECAY 3 · 290 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a soft, plucky pulse.

steps.title: Shimmer
steps.why:
A sixteenth-note echo at 124 BPM is about 120 ms, which fills in the gaps; some feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 4.5 · 120 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 4.5
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: a pulse that shimmers into a hypnotic blur.

sounds.name: Slapback Rockabilly
sounds.ref: In the style of 1950s Sun Records rockabilly
sounds.blurb: A walking rockabilly bass with the quick single slap of a tape echo.
sounds.how: Sun Records used a short tape echo, a single quick repeat called slapback, on almost everything. A short TIME with no feedback.

steps.title: Slap bass
steps.why:
A square with a middle cutoff and a quick DEPTH pluck; a short decay.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 3.5 · 522 Hz
- RESONANCE 1
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 4
- DECAY 2 · 210 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a plucky walking bass.

steps.title: Slapback
steps.why:
About 110 ms with no feedback: one quick repeat right behind each note.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 4 · 110 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 0
- Delay LEVEL 6
- Listen for: the classic rockabilly slap.

context.dly.feedback: Zero: slapback is a single repeat.

sounds.name: Cave Drips
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient field recordings
sounds.blurb: Water dripping in a deep cave, each drip echoing away.
sounds.how: A drip is a short resonant “plip”. With a long echo and high feedback, each one rings around the cave.

steps.title: Plip
steps.why:
Low cutoff, high resonance and plenty of DEPTH: the filter swoops on each note. A short decay.
- WAVE Sawtooth
- CUTOFF 2 · 297 Hz
- RESONANCE 9
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 6
- DECAY 1 · 160 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a liquid plip.

steps.title: Cave
steps.why:
The longest TIME with high feedback, like a big stone space.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 10 · 500 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 7
- Delay LEVEL 5
- MASTER 10: up, because the drips are few and far between
- Listen for: drips echoing around a cave.

sounds.name: Dub Techno Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of Rhythm & Sound
sounds.blurb: A muffled stab that disappears into a haze of echoes.
sounds.how: Berlin dub techno buries a single stab in echo. One short, muffled note per bar and a long, feeding-back delay.

steps.title: Muffled stab
steps.why:
A saw with a low cutoff, some resonance and a quick DEPTH; a short decay.
- WAVE Sawtooth
- CUTOFF 2.5 · 358 Hz
- RESONANCE 5
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 4
- DECAY 1.5 · 190 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a short, muffled stab.

steps.title: Haze
steps.why:
A dotted-eighth echo at 120 BPM is about 375 ms; high feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 8.8 · 370 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 7.5
- Delay LEVEL 6
- MASTER 10: up, because there is only one stab a bar
- Listen for: a stab dissolving into hazy echoes.

sounds.name: Consumed
sounds.ref: In the style of Plastikman — Consumed
sounds.blurb: A dark, slow, sparse bass pulse swallowed by echoes in a black space.
sounds.how: Plastikman’s Consumed is dark, slow minimal techno: sparse low notes, lots of space and long echoes.

steps.title: Dark
steps.why:
A square with a very low cutoff and a little resonance; a medium decay.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 1.5 · 246 Hz
- RESONANCE 3
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 2.5
- DECAY 4 · 380 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a dark, low pulse.

steps.title: Swallowed
steps.why:
A long TIME with medium-high feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 9.5 · 440 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 6
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: sparse pulses swallowed by echo.

tweaks.hear: The echoes louder than the notes.

sounds.name: Starfield
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s space ambient
sounds.blurb: High, twinkling bleeps scattered across a starry sky of echoes.
sounds.how: High square bleeps through a long echo twinkle like stars. A bright filter, a short decay and lots of repeats.

steps.title: Bleep
steps.why:
A square with a bright cutoff and a little resonance; a short decay.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 7 · 1.9 kHz
- RESONANCE 3
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 1
- DECAY 1 · 160 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a clean, high bleep.

steps.title: Stars
steps.why:
A long TIME and high feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 10 · 500 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 7
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: twinkling stars in a sky of echoes.

sounds.name: Echo Throw
sounds.ref: In the style of dub sound-system echo throws
sounds.blurb: A single note thrown into an echo that feeds back and swells.
sounds.how: Dub engineers “throw” a sound into the echo and push the feedback up so it swells and smears. One note, then the delay at its highest feedback.

steps.title: One shot
steps.why:
A saw with a middle cutoff and some resonance; a short decay.
- WAVE Sawtooth
- CUTOFF 4.5 · 760 Hz
- RESONANCE 5
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 3
- DECAY 2 · 210 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a single, short note.

steps.title: Throw
steps.why:
A long TIME, the feedback near the top and the LEVEL high.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 9.4 · 430 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 8.5: near the top, so the echo barely dies
- Delay LEVEL 7
- MASTER 10: up, because there is only one note
- Listen for: the note echoing on and on, swelling and smearing.

context.dly.feedback: Above about 9 the echo would feed itself for ever.

tweaks.hear: The echoes get grittier as they pile up.

sounds.name: Harmonia Echo
sounds.ref: In the style of Harmonia
sounds.blurb: A sweet, simple, sunny melody looping through a friendly echo.
sounds.how: Harmonia (Cluster and Neu!’s Michael Rother) made gentle, sunny pieces from simple repeating figures and echoes.

steps.title: Sweet
steps.why:
A square with a middle cutoff, a little DEPTH; a medium decay.
- WAVE Square
- CUTOFF 4.5 · 760 Hz
- RESONANCE 2
- DEPTH (envelope to filter) 2
- DECAY 3 · 290 ms
- ACCENT 0
- Listen for: a sweet, round tone.

steps.title: Friendly echo
steps.why:
An eighth-note echo at 112 BPM is about 270 ms; moderate feedback.
- DELAY ON/OFF On
- Delay TIME 7.5 · 270 ms
- Delay FEEDBACK 4
- Delay LEVEL 5
- Listen for: a sunny, looping melody with friendly echoes.

sounds.name: Echoing Guitar
